browse.diagnostics.field.set.description: Row label in the playback diagnostics read-out (which television model and board this is). It is right-aligned into a narrow gutter at the dense diagnostic size, so it must stay short (about 12 characters).

browse.diagnostics.field.firmware.description: Row label in the playback diagnostics read-out (the television firmware name and codename). It is right-aligned into a narrow gutter at the dense diagnostic size, so it must stay short (about 12 characters).

browse.diagnostics.field.decoder.description: Row label in the playback diagnostics read-out (which video codecs the hardware decoder supports). It is right-aligned into a narrow gutter at the dense diagnostic size, so it must stay short (about 12 characters).

browse.diagnostics.field.audio.description: Row label in the playback diagnostics read-out (the audio codec chain or audio capabilities). It is right-aligned into a narrow gutter at the dense diagnostic size, so it must stay short (about 12 characters).

browse.diagnostics.field.route.description: Row label in the playback diagnostics read-out (the delivery route: streaming transport and whether the server converts the file). It is right-aligned into a narrow gutter at the dense diagnostic size, so it must stay short (about 12 characters).

browse.diagnostics.field.picture.description: Row label in the playback diagnostics read-out (the decoded picture size and frame rate). It is right-aligned into a narrow gutter at the dense diagnostic size, so it must stay short (about 12 characters).

browse.diagnostics.field.timeline.description: Row label in the playback diagnostics read-out (playback position and duration). It is right-aligned into a narrow gutter at the dense diagnostic size, so it must stay short (about 12 characters).

browse.diagnostics.field.av_sync.description: Row label in the playback diagnostics read-out (how far audio trails video). It is right-aligned into a narrow gutter at the dense diagnostic size, so it must stay short (about 12 characters).

browse.diagnostics.field.video_plane.description: Row label in the playback diagnostics read-out (the television's hardware video layer). It is right-aligned into a narrow gutter at the dense diagnostic size, so it must stay short (about 12 characters).

browse.diagnostics.field.transfer.description: Row label in the playback diagnostics read-out (bytes received from the server). It is right-aligned into a narrow gutter at the dense diagnostic size, so it must stay short (about 12 characters).

browse.diagnostics.field.load.description: Row label in the playback diagnostics read-out (whether the television's media pipeline accepted the stream). It is right-aligned into a narrow gutter at the dense diagnostic size, so it must stay short (about 12 characters).

browse.diagnostics.field.frames.description: Row label in the playback diagnostics read-out (decoded frame count). It is right-aligned into a narrow gutter at the dense diagnostic size, so it must stay short (about 12 characters).

browse.diagnostics.chart.network.description: Uppercase key beside one of the three plots in the playback diagnostics chart (bytes arriving from the network).

browse.diagnostics.chart.buffer.description: Uppercase key beside one of the three plots in the playback diagnostics chart (seconds of media buffered).

browse.diagnostics.build_dev.description: Build kind in the diagnostics header: a developer build with test hooks.

browse.diagnostics.build_release.description: Build kind in the diagnostics header: the build users install.

browse.diagnostics.header.description: Identity line of the diagnostics read-out: app name and version, build kind, TV software, whether the TV supports Dolby Vision (DV), and the drawing surface size in pixels.

browse.diagnostics.dv_yes.description: Diagnostics header: the TV supports Dolby Vision.

browse.diagnostics.dv_no.description: Diagnostics header: the TV does not support Dolby Vision.

browse.diagnostics.dv_supported.description: Diagnostics: the TV reports Dolby Vision support.

browse.diagnostics.dv_unsupported.description: Diagnostics: the TV reports no Dolby Vision support.

browse.diagnostics.dv_forced.description: Diagnostics: the Dolby Vision answer was forced by a test override rather than asked of the TV.

browse.diagnostics.dv_base_layer.description: Diagnostics: a Dolby Vision file is played through its ordinary HDR base layer.

browse.diagnostics.dv_declare.description: Diagnostics: Dolby Vision is declared to the TV for direct play.

browse.diagnostics.dv_refuse.description: Diagnostics: direct play of this Dolby Vision file is refused.

browse.diagnostics.placed.description: Diagnostics: the video layer was placed with this source size; rv is the platform call's technical return value.

browse.diagnostics.no_video_path.description: Diagnostics fault: the app has no way to show video on this TV.

browse.diagnostics.no_audio_payload.description: Diagnostics: the TV was told the stream has no audio; needAudio:false is the literal technical flag.

browse.diagnostics.feed_accepting.description: Diagnostics: the decoder is accepting data.

browse.diagnostics.feed_full.description: Diagnostics: the decoder's buffer is full; BufferFull is the TV's literal status code.

browse.diagnostics.feed_refused.description: Diagnostics fault: the decoder refused data.

browse.diagnostics.feed_holding.description: Diagnostics: feeding is paused on purpose to stay about 1.6 seconds ahead of the picture.

browse.diagnostics.feed_empty.description: Diagnostics: there is no data waiting to be fed.

browse.diagnostics.feed_none.description: Diagnostics: nothing has been fed to the decoder yet.

browse.diagnostics.fed_rate.description: Diagnostics: video frames and audio packets fed per second.

browse.clock.notice_year.value: TV clock looks wrong ({year}). Connected by the remembered key.
browse.clock.notice_year.description: System toast shown once per app run when the app had to recognise the Plex server by its remembered key because the server's certificate failed its date check (most likely because the television's clock is wrong, but an expired certificate on a correct clock engages it too). Hedged on purpose ("looks wrong"): the app cannot know the clock is the cause. {year} is the four-digit year the television believes it is, written as plain digits. The toast wraps at roughly 40 characters per line and shows up to three lines, so keep the whole sentence at 120 characters or fewer and hedge it in every language.

browse.clock.notice.value: TV clock looks wrong. Connected by the remembered key.
browse.clock.notice.description: Same toast as the year variant, for when the television's year is unknown. Keep it at 120 characters or fewer (up to three lines of roughly 40) and hedge it in every language.
